newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares jump at start of fresh settlement.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares jump at start of fresh settlement.

text.p: Delhi shares rose on Monday at the start of a new settlement period but the increase was capped by uncertainty over whether former finance minister P. Chidambaram's party would join the government, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 3.96 points higher at 801.63 points after 30 minutes of trade.
"Despite a rise in share prices, major players were awaiting Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress party's decision to join the government," said Ashok Arya of brokers S.C. Gupta.
The Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) on Sunday authorised its leader, G.K. Moopanar, to decide whether the regional party should join India's new government.

The TMC, part of the centre-left United Front coalition, decided on April 19 to stay out of the government after the alliance chose Inder Kumar Gujral instead of Moopanar as its leader and new prime minister.
The TMC's decision was keenly awaited by investors as Chidambaram is a key economic reformer who presented a tax-cutting budget for 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28.
Gujral has not appointed a finance minister in his cabinet, signalling the slot was open for Chidambaram. The budget has yet to win parliamentary approval.
Reliance Industries rose 6.75 rupees to 304.75 on speculative buying as there would be a no-delivery period of one month in the share, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro increased 0.25 rupee to 227.30.
